reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as an official Kehlani music release with a brand partnership and an ordinary invitation to download or stream the song. The music-video imagery and lyric-like audio are consistent with entertainment content, and no financial solicitation or data request is described.

citations.quote: I love it when we, when we, when we, I love it when we win.

opening.argument: Judge the invitation as a promise tied to an action: viewers are offered access to the song through “Download/stream now!” followed immediately by a link. That makes obtaining a digital item the reason to leave the video. The official-video title lends credibility to the invitation, but neither the title nor the description establishes what happens after a viewer follows the link. The concern is the access pathway, not a claim that the video asks for money.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the music imagery and lyric as dispositive, but they establish the video's entertainment setting, not the destination of its download link. Its observation that no financial solicitation or data request is described is narrower than a finding that the linked access flow is harmless. The invitation to leave the video remains part of what viewers are asked to do.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A link to download or stream a named song is an ordinary part of a music release. The quoted invitation promises no free reward, unusual benefit or withdrawal, and supplies no evidence of a deceptive destination. The official-video title and song-focused description support the straightforward entertainment reading; uncertainty about an unvisited link does not establish a scam.

citations.quote: The official audio of "Touch" by Kehlani.

opening.argument: The risk signal is the concentration of off-video destinations around an immediate call to act. The description says “Download/stream now!” and also urges viewers to subscribe, while presenting a partnership and an official-artist identity. Those authority cues can make a viewer less inclined to examine where a link leads. None of the supplied material verifies the destination or its terms. The judge should therefore avoid treating the music-video presentation alone as proof that the linked acquisition path is benign.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the sampled lyric does not solicit money. But the lyric does not address the description's links, either. Calling the video entertainment explains the footage; it does not verify the destinations attached to the request to download or stream. The absence of a described data request leaves that question unanswered rather than settling it.

citations.quote: I love it when we, when we, when we, I love it when we win.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: External links and artist credentials are expected in a music-video description. “Download/stream now!” identifies the ordinary purpose of the primary link, while the supplied text makes no claim of free money, an unusually easy reward or a verification step. The opening identifies something it cannot check, not evidence that viewers are being deceived.

citations.quote: Subscribe for more official content from Kehlani:

opening.argument: This is not only a song presentation. The description explicitly turns the attention generated by the video toward an action: download or stream the track through its link. It also asks for subscriptions and lists places to follow the artist. The visual performance can supply the appeal, while the description supplies the participation pathway. Judge the whole presentation, including that promotional role, rather than letting the absence of a spoken sales pitch end the inquiry.

citations.quote: Download/stream now! - https://atlantic.lnk.to/touchID Subscribe for more official content from Kehlani:
Follow Kehlani http://kehlanimusic.com https://facebook.com/Kehlanimusic https://twitter.com/Kehlani https://instagram.com/kehlani

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the invitation ordinary, but that is an interpretation of its purpose, not a description of what a viewer encounters after following it. Its music imagery and lyric support the entertainment framing without erasing the explicit download instruction. The question is whether that instruction matters to the assessment, even though the video itself describes no financial or data request.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion is not itself deception. Here the action is to download or stream the named song, with separate invitations to subscribe and follow the artist. The opening shows a music release being promoted but identifies no misleading reward, special acquisition claim or harmful participation requirement. Its promotional reading is compatible with the video's entertainment purpose.
